lines.text: A frog hops around a hexagon at random. How long until it has visited every corner?
lines.caption: A frog hops around a hexagon at random. How long until it has visited every corner?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! A beautiful pattern is hiding here. Let's find it together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! A beautiful pattern is hiding here. Let's find it together.

lines.text: A frog sits on one vertex, or corner, of a regular hexagon.
lines.caption: A frog sits on one vertex, or corner, of a regular hexagon.

lines.text: Each second, it jumps to one of the two neighboring corners, each with chance one half.
lines.caption: Each second, it jumps to one of the two neighboring corners, each with chance one half.

lines.text: What is the expected number of jumps until the frog has been on all six corners?
lines.caption: What is the expected number of jumps until the frog has been on all six corners?

lines.text: Expected number means the average, as if the frog did this a million times.
lines.caption: Expected number means the average, as if the frog did this a million times.

lines.text: The starting corner already counts as visited. So we need five new corners.
lines.caption: The starting corner already counts as visited. So we need five new corners.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: one stage at a time

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's color every corner the frog has visited green.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's color every corner the frog has visited green.

lines.text: The frog only jumps to neighbors. So the green corners always form one unbroken block.
lines.caption: The frog only jumps to neighbors. So the green corners always form one unbroken block.

lines.text: And when the block grows, the frog is standing on the new corner, at an end of the block.
lines.caption: And when the block grows, the frog is standing on the new corner, at an end of the block.

lines.text: To reach a new corner, it must step just outside the block, on either side.
lines.caption: To reach a new corner, it must step just outside the block, on either side.

lines.text: So the trip splits into five stages. In stage two, two corners are green, and so on.
lines.caption: So the trip splits into five stages. In stage two, two corners are green, and so on.

lines.text: Stage one is quick. Both neighbors are new, so it takes exactly one jump.
lines.caption: Stage one is quick. Both neighbors are new, so it takes exactly one jump.

lines.text: Stage two. Let's straighten the hexagon into a line: an exit, the green block, and an exit.
lines.caption: Stage two. Let's straighten the hexagon into a line: an exit, the green block, and an exit.

lines.text: Call W the frog's average waiting time at an end. Every jump costs one. Then add the average waiting time of the two spots it could land on.
lines.caption: Call W the frog's average waiting time at an end. Every jump costs one. Then add the average waiting time of the two spots it could land on.

lines.text: Half the time, it steps off the block. Done! The other half, it lands on the other end.
lines.caption: Half the time, it steps off the block. Done! The other half, it lands on the other end.

lines.text: That end is a mirror image, so its waiting time is also W. So W is one, plus W over two.
lines.caption: That end is a mirror image, so its waiting time is also W. So W is one, plus W over two.

lines.text: Take W over two from both sides. W over two is one, so W is two jumps.
lines.caption: Take W over two from both sides. W over two is one, so W is two jumps.

lines.text: Stage three. The block has an end, a middle, and another end. Call the middle's waiting time M.
lines.caption: Stage three. The block has an end, a middle, and another end. Call the middle's waiting time M.

lines.text: From the middle, every jump lands on an end. So M is one plus W.
lines.caption: From the middle, every jump lands on an end. So M is one plus W.

lines.text: From the end, half the time it's done, and half the time it goes to the middle.
lines.caption: From the end, half the time it's done, and half the time it goes to the middle.

lines.text: So W is one, plus half of M. Swap in one plus W for M.
lines.caption: So W is one, plus half of M. Swap in one plus W for M.

lines.text: W is three over two, plus W over two. So W is three jumps!
lines.caption: W is three over two, plus W over two. So W is three jumps!

lines.text: Stage four has two twin spots in the middle. Call each one's waiting time P.
lines.caption: Stage four has two twin spots in the middle. Call each one's waiting time P.

lines.text: From P, it goes to the end or its twin. So P is one, plus W over two, plus P over two.
lines.caption: From P, it goes to the end or its twin. So P is one, plus W over two, plus P over two.

lines.text: So P is two more than W. And W is one plus P over two. Solve it: W is four jumps!
lines.caption: So P is two more than W. And W is one plus P over two. Solve it: W is four jumps!

lines.text: Stage five: only one corner is missing. It touches both ends, so both exits land on it.
lines.caption: Stage five: only one corner is missing. It touches both ends, so both exits land on it.

lines.text: Same trick, with one more letter. It works out to waiting times of five at the ends, eight next to them, and nine in the middle.
lines.caption: Same trick, with one more letter. It works out to waiting times of five at the ends, eight next to them, and nine in the middle.

lines.text: Add the five stages: one plus two plus three plus four plus five.
lines.caption: Add the five stages: one plus two plus three plus four plus five.

lines.text: The answer is <short pause> fifteen! Choice C.
lines.caption: The answer is fifteen! Choice C.

lines.text: Why does it go one, two, three, four, five? Let's draw stage five's waiting times as bars.
lines.caption: Why does it go one, two, three, four, five? Let's draw stage five's waiting times as bars.

lines.text: The exits wait zero. Each other spot waits one more than the average of its neighbors.
lines.caption: The exits wait zero. Each other spot waits one more than the average of its neighbors.

lines.text: The waiting times are zero, five, eight, nine, eight, five, zero. Check one: eight is one plus seven.
lines.caption: The waiting times are zero, five, eight, nine, eight, five, zero. Check one: eight is one plus seven.

lines.text: Now look at the climbs: up five, up three, up one, down one, down three, down five.
lines.caption: Now look at the climbs: up five, up three, up one, down one, down three, down five.

lines.text: Halfway between five and nine is seven. Eight is one above, so climbing in beats climbing out by two.
lines.caption: Halfway between five and nine is seven. Eight is one above, so climbing in beats climbing out by two.

lines.text: And look again. Five is one times five, eight is two times four, nine is three times three.
lines.caption: And look again. Five is one times five, eight is two times four, nine is three times three.

lines.text: Each waiting time is the steps to one exit, times the steps to the other exit!
lines.caption: Each waiting time is the steps to one exit, times the steps to the other exit!

lines.text: Stage k has k plus one climbs, shrinking by two. Both exits are zero, so the climbs cancel: they run from up k to down k.
lines.caption: Stage k has k plus one climbs, shrinking by two. Both exits are zero, so the climbs cancel: they run from up k to down k.

lines.text: So the frog at an end, one step from one exit and k from the other, waits k jumps.
lines.caption: So the frog at an end, one step from one exit and k from the other, waits k jumps.

lines.text: When would you pick this one? When the shape gets big, and solving equations gets long.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? When the shape gets big, and solving equations gets long.

lines.text: A, ten, is what you'd get if you stopped after stage four. The last stage still needs five.
lines.caption: A, ten, is what you'd get if you stopped after stage four. The last stage still needs five.

lines.text: B, twelve, and D, eighteen, give every corner the same cost, two or three. But the stages aren't equal.
lines.caption: B, twelve, and D, eighteen, give every corner the same cost, two or three. But the stages aren't equal.

lines.text: They grow, because a step back lands INSIDE the block, farther from new corners.
lines.caption: They grow, because a step back lands INSIDE the block, farther from new corners.

lines.text: E, twenty-one, counts a sixth stage. Once all six corners are green, the frog is done!
lines.caption: E, twenty-one, counts a sixth stage. Once all six corners are green, the frog is done!

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same frog, same rules, but on a regular octagon with eight corners.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same frog, same rules, but on a regular octagon with eight corners.

lines.text: What is the expected number of jumps until it has been on all eight corners?
lines.caption: What is the expected number of jumps until it has been on all eight corners?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: The green corners still form one block, and each stage starts at an end.
lines.caption: The green corners still form one block, and each stage starts at an end.

lines.text: With k corners green, the waiting time is one times k. That's k jumps.
lines.caption: With k corners green, the waiting time is one times k. That's k jumps.

lines.text: Seven new corners, seven stages: one plus two, up to seven. That's twenty-eight jumps!
lines.caption: Seven new corners, seven stages: one plus two, up to seven. That's twenty-eight jumps!

lines.text: The big idea: picture a walker on a line, with equal chances each step, and an exit at each end.
lines.caption: The big idea: picture a walker on a line, with equal chances each step, and an exit at each end.

lines.text: Its average wait to step off is the steps to one exit, times the steps to the other.
lines.caption: Its average wait to step off is the steps to one exit, times the steps to the other.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
